So while much of the area surrounding the site may suffer from a projected sea level rise of 7.2 feet by the year 2100, the T-RICH site will not since it is significantly higher than most of the surrounding port and region which will insulate it from such negative effects. A topographical survey based on the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 shows that the site’s native elevation ranges from 8.1 feet at the southwest corner to 17.6 feet in the eastern half. After it is filled and graded for use as the T-RICH facility, it is projected to be 13.5 feet throughout the center drainage basin to 14.5 feet near the perimeter. Therefore, all CO handling equipment, buildings, and infrastructure will be located well above 2 the projected 7.2 foot level by 2100. Note that in the Tampa Bay region, an elevation of 0 feet relative to the NAVD88 system is 1.48 feet higher than mean lower-low water (MLLW). Therefore, the site’s NAVD88 elevation of 14 feet is actually 15.48 feet above MLLW, providing an even greater margin of safety. Storm surge due to hurricanes and other severe weather events is a greater threat to the site in the foreseeable future than long-term sea level rise. Scientists generally agree that climate change is producing more frequent and more severe destructive storms including tornados and hurricanes, both of which have appeared in Florida more regularly in recent years.
